chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) used to, when he reached the Hijr (area near the Kaaba) before reaching the Mizab (spout of the Kaaba), raise his head and say: 'O Allah, admit me into Paradise by Your mercy, and grant me health from illness, and expand for me from lawful sustenance, and avert from me the evil of the wicked of the Jinn and humans, and the evil of the wicked of the Arabs and non-Arabs.'

key_terms.الْحِجْر: The semi-circular wall area near the Kaaba
key_terms.الْمِيزَاب: The golden spout of the Kaaba
key_terms.عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ: Peace be upon them both (referring to Imam and his father)
key_terms.فَسَقَةِ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ: The wicked/deviant of the Jinn and humans

ai.seo_question: What was the specific supplication of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn during Tawaf?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the specific devotional practice of Imam Zayn al-Abidin, who paused between the Hijr al-Aswad and the Mizab (the gutter of the Kaaba) to recite a comprehensive supplication. This location is significant in Shia jurisprudence as a recommended spot for du'a during Tawaf, emphasizing the integration of spiritual petition with the physical rituals of pilgrimage. The supplication reflects a holistic request for divine mercy, covering both worldly needs like lawful sustenance and health, and spiritual protection from the evil of Jinn and humans.
